source_metadata.title: Heparin Resistance in SARS-CoV-2 Infected Patients with Venous Thromboembolism
source_metadata.design: IRB-approved retrospective medication-use evaluation / retrospective cohort

atoms.canonical_statement: The study evaluated whether COVID-19-positive patients with confirmed VTE required more IV UFH to achieve therapeutic anticoagulation under anti-Xa monitoring than COVID-19-negative patients.
This was an IRB-approved retrospective medication-use evaluation/cohort study of IV UFH during the first COVID-19 wave from March through June 2020.
Eligible patients were adults with radiographically confirmed VTE treated with IV UFH during March-June 2020.

population.label: Adults with radiographically confirmed VTE treated with IV UFH

atoms.canonical_statement: Pregnancy and targeted temperature management were exclusion criteria because they may alter heparin pharmacokinetics.

population.label: Study candidates

atoms.canonical_statement: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation was an exclusion criterion because it may increase the risk of heparin resistance.

population.label: Study candidates

atoms.canonical_statement: Patients with fewer than three anti-Xa levels or less than 24 hours of IV UFH infusion were excluded.

population.label: Study candidates

atoms.canonical_statement: Patients who received a direct oral anticoagulant before IV UFH initiation were excluded to avoid DOAC interference with the heparin anti-Xa assay.

population.label: Study candidates
exclusion_criteria: Direct oral anticoagulant before IV UFH initiation

atoms.canonical_statement: Anti-Xa values <0.3 units/mL were defined as subtherapeutic, 0.3-0.7 units/mL as therapeutic, and >0.7 units/mL as supratherapeutic.

outcome.definition: <0.3 units/mL subtherapeutic; 0.3-0.7 units/mL therapeutic; >0.7 units/mL supratherapeutic

atoms.canonical_statement: The primary outcome was the IV UFH dose required to achieve anti-Xa ≥0.3 units/mL in COVID-19-positive versus COVID-19-negative patients.

concept.text: IV UFH dose to first anti-Xa ≥0.3 units/mL

outcome.definition: UFH infusion dose at first anti-Xa value ≥0.3 units/mL

atoms.canonical_statement: Secondary outcomes included time and dose adjustments to anti-Xa ≥0.3 units/mL, UFH dose and dose adjustments to the 0.3-0.7 units/mL therapeutic range, time to therapeutic range, and bleeding.
Categorical and continuous comparisons used Chi-square/Fisher exact tests and the Mann-Whitney U test, respectively, as appropriate.
All anti-Xa laboratory analyses used the same ACL TOP 750 CTS analyzer and HemosIL Liquid Anti-Xa reagent.
The institutional VTE protocol allowed an optional IV UFH bolus of 80 units/kg and started the infusion at 18 units/kg/hour using actual body weight; dose capping was at provider discretion.

exposures.details: Optional 80 units/kg bolus; actual body weight dosing; dose capping at provider discretion

atoms.canonical_statement: Anti-Xa levels were obtained 6 hours after UFH initiation and every 6 hours thereafter until two consecutive therapeutic values, after which monitoring was daily.

For patients not reaching anti-Xa ≥0.3 units/mL within 24 hours, clinically significant heparin resistance was defined by a requirement for >35,000 units/day of IV UFH to achieve the target or >35,000 units/day with failure to achieve it.

outcome.definition: Among patients unable to achieve anti-Xa ≥0.3 units/mL within 24 h: >35,000 units/day to achieve target, or >35,000 units/day and unable to achieve target

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors concluded that, with anti-Xa monitoring, UFH dosage requirements and time to therapeutic anticoagulation appeared similar between COVID-19-positive and COVID-19-negative patients with confirmed VTE.
The authors stated that COVID-19 patients may be successfully anticoagulated with IV UFH using anti-Xa monitoring, while clinically significant heparin resistance may still occur.
The authors called for further studies to strengthen recommendations favoring anti-Xa over aPTT monitoring and to better define heparin resistance in COVID-19.
The small sample size may have increased the risk of a Type II error.
Requiring at least 24 hours of UFH infusion may have missed heparin-resistant patients who were switched early to alternative anticoagulants after low initial anti-Xa values.
Inflammatory markers were not routinely obtained in COVID-19-negative patients, preventing direct inflammatory-marker comparisons between groups.
The study evaluated first-wave COVID-19 in the northeastern United States from March-June 2020, so findings may not generalize to later viral variants.
The study did not evaluate ongoing UFH doses required to maintain anti-Xa ≥0.3 units/mL, so heparin resistance developing later in hospitalization may have been missed.

The >35,000 units/day heparin-resistance threshold has not been validated in clinical trials and is strongly influenced by body weight; standard 18 units/kg/hour dosing can exceed this threshold in heavier patients.
Full ISTH criteria for major bleeding and clinically relevant non-major bleeding could not be collected because of the retrospective study design.
The authors declared no potential conflicts of interest related to the research, authorship, or publication of the article.
The authors reported receiving no financial support for the research, authorship, or publication of the article.

extraction_limitations: Extraction was limited to the uploaded primary article; cited references were not atomized.
The article contained three main tables and no main-text figures; table-derived atoms were anchored to table/row locators.
Some medians with IQRs contain two group-specific IQRs; the canonical statement preserves both, while the structured interval field represents the COVID-19-positive estimate and its IQR.
Bleeding could not be classified using full ISTH major/clinically relevant non-major bleeding criteria because the source itself reported those data were unavailable.
No data-availability statement was identified in the article, so no data_availability atom was created.
Atoms are machine-extracted and marked extracted, not human-verified.
